## Calculated Values {#sec-calculated}

Parameters derived from mathematical formulas and economic models.

### Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH: $27.2B {#sec-treaty_annual_funding}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual funding from 1% of global military spending redirected to DIH

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [1% Reduction in Military Spending/War Costs from Treaty](#sec-treaty_reduction_pct): 1%

$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### US Discretionary Efficiency: 40.5% {#sec-us_fed_discretionary_efficiency}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US federal discretionary spending efficiency. What fraction of discretionary spending avoids direct waste (Cat 1 only: military overspend, corporate welfare, drug war, fossil/ag subsidies). ~41%. Some Cat 1 items (farm subsidies, tax expenditures) are technically mandatory/off-budget but are fungible policy choices.

**Inputs**:

- [Category 1: Direct Spending Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_category_1_direct_spending) 🔢: $1.01T
- [US Federal Discretionary Spending (FY2024)](#sec-us_fed_discretionary_spending_2024) 📊: $1.70T

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_{US,disc} \\
= 1 - \frac{W_{cat1}}{Spending_{fed}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$1.01T}{\$1.7T} \\
= 40.5\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat1} \\
= W_{military} + W_{corporate} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$615B + \$181B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$1.01T
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

### US Governance Efficiency (GDP): 83% {#sec-us_governance_efficiency_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total US governance efficiency: all 4 waste categories as share of GDP. 1 - ($4.9T / $28.78T) = ~83%. This broader metric captures direct spending waste, compliance burden, policy-induced GDP loss, and system inefficiency relative to total economic output.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.90T
- [US GDP (2024)](#sec-us_gdp_2024) 📊: $28.8T

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_{US,GDP} \\
= 1 - \frac{W_{total,US}}{USGDP} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$4.9T}{\$28.8T} \\
= 83\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

### Category 1: Direct Spending Waste: $1.01T {#sec-us_gov_waste_category_1_direct_spending}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Category 1: Direct Federal Spending Waste. Actual federal budget allocations that could be redirected. Includes military overspend ($615B), corporate welfare ($181B), drug war ($90B), fossil fuel subsidies ($50B), and agricultural subsidies ($75B). Total: ~$1.01T annually. Solution: Budget reallocation.

**Inputs**:

- [Military Overspend](#sec-us_gov_waste_military_overspend) 📊: $615B (95% CI: $500B - $750B)
- [Corporate Welfare Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_corporate_welfare) 📊: $181B (95% CI: $150B - $220B)
- [Drug War Cost](#sec-us_gov_waste_drug_war) 📊: $90B (95% CI: $60B - $150B)
- [Fossil Fuel Subsidies (Explicit)](#sec-us_gov_waste_fossil_fuel_subsidies) 📊: $50B (95% CI: $30B - $80B)
- [Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss](#sec-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies) 📊: $75B (95% CI: $50B - $120B)

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat1} \\
= W_{military} + W_{corporate} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$615B + \$181B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$1.01T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Category 2: Compliance Burden: $1.13T {#sec-us_gov_waste_category_2_compliance}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Category 2: Compliance Burden on Private Sector. Private sector resources consumed by government-imposed compliance requirements. Includes tax compliance ($546B) and regulatory red tape ($580B). Total: ~$1.13T annually. Solution: Simplification (tax code reform, regulatory streamlining).

**Inputs**:

- [Tax Compliance Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_tax_compliance) 📊: $546B (95% CI: $450B - $650B)
- [Regulatory Red Tape Waste](#sec-us_gov_waste_regulatory_red_tape) 📊: $580B (95% CI: $290B - $1T)

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat2} \\
= W_{tax} + W_{regulatory} \\
= \$546B + \$580B \\
= \$1.13T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Category 3: GDP Loss: $1.56T {#sec-us_gov_waste_category_3_gdp_loss}

Category 3: Policy-Induced GDP Loss. Economic output foregone due to policy constraints on markets. Includes housing/zoning restrictions ($1.4T) and tariffs ($160B). Total: ~$1.56T annually. Solution: Policy reform (zoning liberalization, trade policy).

**Inputs**:

- [Housing/Zoning Restrictions Cost](#sec-us_gov_waste_housing_zoning) 📊: $1.40T (95% CI: $500B - $2T)
- [Tariff Cost (GDP Loss)](#sec-us_gov_waste_tariffs) 📊: $160B (95% CI: $90B - $250B)

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{cat3} \\
= W_{housing} + W_{tariffs} \\
= \$1.4T + \$160B \\
= \$1.56T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Category 4: System Inefficiency: $1.20T {#sec-us_gov_waste_category_4_system}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Category 4: Total System Inefficiency. Fundamental system design failures requiring structural redesign. Currently only healthcare system inefficiency ($1.2T). Solution: System redesign using competitive market models (Singapore's catastrophic coverage + HSAs, Switzerland's regulated competition).

**Inputs**:

- [Healthcare System Inefficiency](#sec-us_gov_waste_healthcare_inefficiency) 📊: $1.20T (95% CI: $1T - $1.50T)

$$
W_{cat4} = W_{health} = \$1.2T = \$1.2T
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### US Waste (% GDP): 17% {#sec-us_gov_waste_pct_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US government waste as percentage of GDP. ~$4.90T waste / $28.78T GDP = ~17%. This represents the 'dysfunction tax' that American citizens effectively pay through inefficient governance.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.90T
- [US GDP (2024)](#sec-us_gdp_2024) 📊: $28.8T

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{US,\%GDP} \\
= \frac{W_{total,US}}{USGDP} \\
= \frac{\$4.9T}{\$28.8T} \\
= 17\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

### Recoverable Capital: $2.45T {#sec-us_gov_waste_recoverable}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Recoverable capital if US improved to OECD median efficiency. Current US efficiency ~38-48%; OECD median ~75-85%. Closing to ~80% would recover approximately half the gap.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.90T

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{US,recoverable} \\
= W_{total,US} \times 0.5 \\
= \$4.9T \times 0.5 \\
= \$2.45T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
*? Low confidence*

### Efficiency Gap / Treaty Funding: 180:1 {#sec-us_gov_waste_vs_treaty_multiplier}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

How many times the US government efficiency gap could fund the 1% Treaty. The efficiency gap represents capital that could fund transformative health research many times over.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.90T
- [Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH](#sec-treaty_annual_funding) 🔢: $27.2B

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{waste:treaty} \\
= \frac{W_{total,US}}{Funding_{treaty}} \\
= \frac{\$4.9T}{\$27.2B} \\
= 180
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{total,US} \\
= W_{raw,US} \times US \\
= \$4.9T \times 1 \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} + W_{regulatory} \\
+ W_{tax} + W_{corporate} + W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} \\
+ W_{fossil} + W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B + \$181B + \$160B \\
+ \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/tornado-us_gov_waste_vs_treaty_multiplier.qmd >}}

### Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss: $75B {#sec-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Deadweight loss from US agricultural subsidies. Direct subsidies ~$30B/yr but create larger distortions: overproduction, environmental damage, benefits concentrated in large farms (top 10% receive 78% of subsidies). Total welfare loss ~$75B. Textbook example of capture; very high economist consensus. [CATEGORY 1: Direct Spending]

**Source**: [@ewg-farm-subsidies]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$50B, $120B] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $25B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $50B and $120B (±47%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence*

### Overlap Discount Factor: 1:1 {#sec-us_gov_waste_overlap_discount}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Overlap discount factor between US government waste categories. Set to 1.0 (no discount). Categories are treated as additive, recognizing that any overlap is offset by excluded categories (state/local inefficiency, implicit subsidies, behavioral effects).

```{=html}
<script>
// Conservative lazy loading: only load images actually in viewport
(function() {
  'use strict';
  
  let imageObserver = null;
  let loadTimeout = null;
  
  function enableLazyLoading() {
    const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
    
    // Use Intersection Observer with conservative threshold
    // rootMargin: '50px' means only load images within 50px of viewport
    // This prevents loading images passed through during hash navigation
    imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio > 0) {
          const img = entry.target;
          // Only load if image is actually visible (not just passed through)
          if (img.dataset.src) {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.removeAttribute('data-src');
          } else if (!img.hasAttribute('loading')) {
            // For images without data-src, use native lazy loading
            img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          }
          observer.unobserve(img);
        }
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: '50px',  // Only load images within 50px of viewport
      threshold: 0.01      // Trigger when at least 1% visible
    });
    
    images.forEach(img => {
      imageObserver.observe(img);
    });
  }
  
  // Handle hash navigation (clicking links to sections)
  // Delay loading to avoid loading images passed through during jump
  function handleHashNavigation() {
    if (loadTimeout) clearTimeout(loadTimeout);
    // Wait 300ms after navigation to let scroll settle
    // Images will load naturally via Intersection Observer when visible
    loadTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      // Scroll has settled, Intersection Observer will handle visible images
      // No action needed - observer is already watching
    }, 300);
  }
  
  // Initialize on page load
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enableLazyLoading);
  } else {
    enableLazyLoading();
  }
  
  // Handle hash changes (clicking anchor links)
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', handleHashNavigation);
  
  // Also handle initial hash if page loads with one
  if (window.location.hash) {
    setTimeout(handleHashNavigation, 100);
  }
})();
</script>
```
